title: Empirical-potential reset (ireset 2)
purpose: Exercises `ireset 2` of the `epsr` engine [@soper1996,@soper2005]: the empirical potential is set to zero and any repulsive-core amplitudes `pcoefex` are cleared, while the reference potential, the EP amplitude `ereq` and the configuration are kept. Users take this route to restart a refinement without losing the equilibrated box [@epsrmanual].
fortran: `epsr_standalone_rev3.f`: `runepsr17` (`ireset` = 2 branch, reset after the run), `inita` (accumulators restarted), `generate_ep`, `ptgnsq`
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. The EP is rebuilt from zero during the three runs at `ereq` = 10 kJ/mol. Unlike `ireset 1`, the `.pcof` pair table, `ereq` and the automatic-control settings are kept, and the leading coefficient of each pair is not reset.
inputs: Copy of EPSR-test with only `ireset 2` (instead of 0) in `200DMSO400Water.EPSR.inp`.
verification: Three chained passes; the Fortran writes `ireset 0` after pass 1, so passes 2-3 continue normally from the reset potential. In the Fortran reference `ereq` stays 10, the `.erg` history restarts (3 lines after pass 3) and new EP coefficients are refined from zero. All 27 output files are identical after every pass.
notes: All `pcoefex` are already 0 in EPSR-test, so the clearing of the repulsive cores is executed but has no visible effect in this case.
